questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the son of B’; ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; and, ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is M related to T if ‘M # N @ L × P + T’?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
‘A + B’ means ‘A is the son of B’;
‘A # B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’;
‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; and,
‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’.
Based on the above, how is M related to T if ‘M # N @ L × P + T’?
questions.solution:
M is the sister of N, N is the father of L, L is the wife of P and P is the son of T.

S, M is the 'Son’s wife’s father’s sister' of T.

questions.question: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged? 229 ÷ 41 + 502 × 2 − 44 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?
229 ÷ 41 + 502 × 2 − 44 = ?
questions.solution:
After interchanging the signs then:

⇒ 229 × 41 - 502 ÷ 2 + 44 = ? ⇒ ? = 229 × 41 - 251 + 44 = ? ⇒ ? = 9389 - 251 + 44 ⇒ ? = 9433 - 251 = 9182

questions.question: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 4 – 5 ÷ 9 + 6 × 2 = ?

4 – 5 ÷ 9 + 6 × 2 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 4 – 5 ÷ 9 + 6 × 2 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘-’ and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 4 + 5 × 9 – 6 ÷ 2 = ? ⇒ 4 + 45 – 3 = ? ⇒ 49 - 3 = 46.
